name: aida_r5_dining_can_grasp
purpose: Aida R5 picks up the red Coca-Cola can from the dining table, from its arms-down rest: approach planned by HomeHero's R5 grasp planner (hull candidates, opposition ranking, pinocchio IK, coal screening), close/lift/hold appended open-loop

robot.drive_overrides_why: HomeHero's hand gains; the USD ships hand damping 0.05/rad, which made the fingers oscillate (docs/aida_r5_retention_repair.md); armature 0.005 as HomeHero's hand actuator config (commission_aida_r5.py)

ability_hand.why: the real hand's four-bars (q2 = 1.0585 q1) as mimic joints, so a load on a fingertip reaches its motor; silicone pads as compliant contact (3 kN/m: a few mm of pad and finger give under a few newtons), where a halted digit's squeeze is stored while its worm holds it; silicone friction

objects.name: Target
objects.label: the red Coca-Cola can
objects.physics_why: a full 355 ml can (the library's 0.5 kg is rounded up); friction and solver settings as HomeHero's pickup object

grasp_plan.via_why: HomeHero's planner starts from its reset pose; rest -> reset by its RRT
grasp_plan.hover_clearance_why: HomeHero's 0.14 m hover over the object's top is out of the R5's reach here: 0.985 m needed, 0.978 m reachable from the reset pose (shoulder lift at its stop, then the upper arm meets the chassis). 0.12 m keeps the open fingers (hanging about 0.1 m below the palm) above the can

close.why: the real hand closes on a grip command: every digit driven toward closed and stopped by its own firmware on contact (halt-on-collision), not to planned angles

grasp_replay.why: targets planned by plan_er_grasp.py: the close, lift and hold are already in them
grasp_replay.controller_why: HomeHero's recordings and planner paths are commands to its R5 action layer (gravity-compensated arm targets, gravity feed-forward elsewhere); plain targets leave the shoulder slide 7.5 mm under its target (7.6 kg on 10 kN/m)

hand_model.why: PSYONIC ICD: halt-on-collision at word 007 (3.0 V, the default); word 008 at 1.5 V, mid-range of the ICD's 1-2 V, keeps a small current flowing after contact so the digits close in if the can shifts; grip speed 0xFF (full)

physics_hz_why: the Ability Hand firmware runs once per physics step: 480 Hz is a 2 ms stall-detection loop, and a digit closing at its 8 rad/s top speed moves 1 degree per step
